record.context_brief: Aztec rectangle with a near-central square removed
record.original_question: Find a formula for the number of domino tilings of a (2n-1)-by-2n Aztec rectangle after deleting one of the four squares adjacent to the central square.

evidence.quote: What about (2n − 1)-by-2n rectangles? For these regions, removing the central square does not make the region tilable. However, if one removes any one of the four squares adjacent to the middle square, one obtains a region that is tilable, and moreover, for this region the number of tilings appears to be a nice round number.
Problem 10: Find a formula for the number of domino tilings of a (2n − 1)-by-2n Aztec rectangle with a square adjoining the central square removed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a positive integer $n$, the $(2n-1)$-by-$2n$ Aztec rectangle is the union of unit squares in the plane defined as follows: take the lattice region consisting of all unit squares $[i,i+1]\times[j,j+1]$ with $0\le i\le 2n-1$ and $0\le j\le 2n-2$ (so the region has $2n-1$ rows of length $2n$), arranged in the staircase fashion of an Aztec rectangle (i.e., the rows are successively offset so as to form the standard Aztec rectangle shape with axis $2n-1$ short side and $2n$ long side). The region has a well-defined central unit square. Removing the central square itself yields a region with no domino tiling, but removing any one of the four unit squares sharing an edge with the central square yields a region that admits domino tilings.

Find a closed-form formula, as a function of $n$, for the number of domino tilings (coverings by $1\times 2$ dominoes) of the $(2n-1)$-by-$2n$ Aztec rectangle with one of the four unit squares adjacent to the central square removed.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was resolved by Helfgott and Gessel in "Enumeration of Tilings of Diamonds and Hexagons with Defects" (1998), which gives a closed-form evaluation for the number of tilings of the (2n−1)-by-2n Aztec rectangle with a square adjoining the central square removed, via determinant evaluations.

status_evidence.title: Enumeration of Tilings of Diamonds and Hexagons with Defects (Helfgott–Gessel)
status_evidence.snippet: Counts tilings of Aztec diamonds and hexagons with defects using determinants, including solutions to problems from Propp's list.
status_evidence.claim: Helfgott and Gessel solve Propp's Problem 10 on the (2n−1)-by-2n Aztec rectangle with a square adjacent to the central square removed.

status_evidence.title: Enumeration of Tilings of Diamonds and Hexagons with Defects (Electronic J. Combinatorics)
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of the Helfgott–Gessel paper providing closed-form formulas for several tiling problems with defects from Propp's open problem list.
status_evidence.claim: The formula for Problem 10 is established in this published work.
